# Toggle

A button that stays pressed or not.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Accessible first</span></p>

## When to use it

**In Accessible first:** Turning a mode on and off, with a word on the button. Not a form answer or a one-off action.

- **Use it when:** Turning a mode or format on and off in a toolbar, such as bold.
- **Not when:** A setting saved at once (switch), or a one-off action (button).

Instead:

- [Switch](./switch.md): A setting.
- [Button](./button.md): A one-off action.
- [Toggle group](./toggle-group.md): Several toggles together.

## Why it works this way

Toggle looks the way it does because of 4 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Toggle, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-human-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How do people recall the interface?</b><code>human.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">They see it fresh each time</div><p>Nobody remembers the interface from last time.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toggle</h5><ul><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>default</b>: Every action looks like a control people can find, so the toggle keeps its border.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Button: secondary</code> <code>Button: ghost</code> <code>Button: disabled</code> <code>Field: responsive</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Toggle decisions would reopen</small><p>and 1 answer that follow from it: <b>Actions and status</b>.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-elevation-definition"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What separates groups on the page?</b><code>elevation.definition</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Lines</div><p>Strong borders separate groups at any zoom.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toggle</h5><ul><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>default</b>: Every action looks like a control people can find, so the toggle keeps its border.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>outline</b>: Every toggle, with a strong border and a word, so it reads as a control at any zoom.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Item: default</code> <code>Item: outline</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Toggle decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-iconography-roles"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What do icons do?</b><code>iconography.roles</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Actions and status</div><p>Icons support words; they never replace them.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toggle</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>outline</b>: Every toggle, with a strong border and a word, so it reads as a control at any zoom.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Button: icon</code> <code>Input group: inline-end</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Toggle decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-accessibility-values"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is the smallest target?</b><code>accessibility.values</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Large</div><p>Large targets for tremor and touch.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toggle</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>default</b>: Every toggle. Large targets help people with motor needs.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>sm</b>: Large targets help people with motor needs; nothing smaller.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>lg</b>: The default size is already large for motor needs; a bigger one adds nothing.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Button: default</code> <code>Button: compact</code> <code>Button: large</code> <code>Item: default</code> <code>Item: sm</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">3</div><small>Toggle decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Use common words. Explain any term you must use.
- One idea per sentence. Put the action first.
- Never blame the person.
- Use: Continue, Change, Start, You. Avoid: Invalid, Utilise, Submit, Error code.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Continue
- `content.action.cancel`: Go back
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Start a new application

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| undefined | Space or Enter presses it. | undefined |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It says whether it is pressed. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add toggle
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.
